summary: Path utility that returns a pointer to the final path component by scanning backward from the end of a NUL-terminated string for the last backslash (ASCII 92). The ABI legacy name records it as extracting a filename from a path. It is called once, from SessionConfigBuilder at 0x00461610. With no backslash present the string start is returned.

operations.description: result = &a1[strlen(a1)]: positions a scan pointer at the terminating NUL of the input path string.
if (result > a1): only scan backward when the string is non-empty; an empty string returns the start pointer immediately.
Scan backward while *result != 92 (backslash); on each iteration decrement `result` and return the string start when the pointer reaches the beginning.
On finding a backslash, ++result advances just past it and the function returns the pointer to the path's final component (filename after the last backslash).

unresolved: The packet does not document how SessionConfigBuilder (0x00461610) consumes the returned filename pointer.
With no backslash in the path the function returns the string start; this boundary behavior is unconfirmed to match the caller's expectations.
